name: The Eternal Buffer
premise: You are a midnight archivist mending an infinite, glitching manuscript of reality in a glowing modal editor. Motions carve clean signal from rot, operators stitch broken folios, and a stray cat named Tilde naps on your statusline.
voice: Warm, dryly witty, bookish-weird. Nocturnal archivist meets antique Unix terminal. Short sentences with tactile physical details and cheeky Vim lore.
player: Someone who enjoys active keyboard-driven incrementals over long desk sittings and wants to build real Vim muscle memory slowly and delightfully.

visitor.name: Margin Moth
visitor.line: Tilde bats a glowing moth loose from the gutter.

surface.line: An amber phosphor monitor printing onto coarse Bayer-dithered soot: a warm 4x4 ordered-dither light pool breathes around your Vim cursor, ripples outward on Clean Cuts, thickens with Flow, and casts dot-screen light behind every ASCII panel.

look.moment: Typing :wq to Rebind the Codex for the first time literally writes-and-quits the buffer: every line collapses into Bayer-dithered amber dust under a sweeping raster curtain, Tilde pads across the blank void leaving a glowing ~ trail, and the archive reboots into a richer dual-split strata.
